current_term: Flat $1,550,000/yr Annual Commitment for all 5 years, regardless of consumption.
target_term: Milestone-based ramp: ~$350,000 effective Year 1 (already true), stepping to ~$950,000 in Year 2 aligned to Phase 2 build/MVP, reaching full $1,550,000+ only once the first production use case goes live.
buyer_ask: Replace the flat $1,550,000/yr Annual Commitment with a milestone-based ramp: $350,000 in Year 1 (already effectively true), stepping to $950,000 in Year 2 aligned to the Phase 2 build/MVP window, and reaching full $1,550,000+ only once the first production use case goes live.
negotiation_language: We paid for a full production-scale commitment starting month one, but our own program plan does not reach production until Q1 2027. We are not asking for a discount -- we are asking the payment schedule to match the plan you already have visibility into from our QBRs.
vendor_give: A restructured, lower Year 1/early-Year 2 commitment with the same total 5-year value preserved (or extended by one year), avoiding an outright TCV reduction Databricks has to book against quota.
timing_dependency: Must land before the Oct 14 2026 Year 2 invoice is issued.
risk_if_ignored: A second $1,891,000 payment locks in on the same flat schedule, doubling the sunk-cost exposure before the program has a single production workload.

current_term: Business Critical Support fixed at 22% of the Committed Purchase Amount ($341,000/yr), independent of actual usage.
target_term: Support fee re-based to 22% of actual consumed spend, or Premium-tier economics until consumption crosses ~$500,000 annualized, then step up to Business Critical.
buyer_ask: Re-base Business Critical Support fee to 22% of actual consumed spend rather than committed spend -- or, alternatively, accept Premium-tier support economics until consumption crosses a defined threshold (e.g. $500,000 annualized), then step up to Business Critical.
negotiation_language: We are paying enterprise support pricing for a workload with four support tickets a quarter. Tie the support fee to what we are actually running, and we will happily step it up the moment usage does.
vendor_give: Support tier commitment stays intact on paper (protects Databricks' support-attach metrics) while the fee base shifts to consumption.
timing_dependency: Best attached to the same Year 2 renegotiation window.
risk_if_ignored: Support fee continues accruing against a five-year $1,705,000 total regardless of actual operational load.

current_term: No carry-forward: unused Annual Commitment forfeits at each Contract Year anniversary (Section 2 of the Order Form).
target_term: Carry-forward of unused Annual Commitment for up to 12 months past the Contract Year anniversary, applied retroactively to the ~$1,483,900 of Year 1 headroom.
buyer_ask: Amend Section 2 of the Order Form to add carry-forward of unused Annual Commitment for up to 12 months past the Contract Year anniversary, applied retroactively to the ~$1,483,900 of Year 1 headroom.
negotiation_language: You have not lost this money -- we have not spent it yet. A carry-forward provision costs you nothing you were not already going to receive; it just stops converting a timing gap into a forfeiture.
vendor_give: No cash cost to Databricks; it is a scheduling concession, which is why it is a strong first ask.
timing_dependency: Must be signed before Oct 14 2026 or Year 1 headroom forfeits automatically per the current clause.
risk_if_ignored: ~$1.48M of already-paid, unconsumed Year 1 commitment is simply gone at the anniversary -- the single largest dollar exposure in this file.

current_term: Commitment paid directly to Databricks; no AWS Marketplace routing.
target_term: Year 2-forward commitment routed through an AWS Marketplace private offer, retiring AWS EDP commitment with the same dollars.
buyer_ask: Route the Year 2-forward commitment through an AWS Marketplace private offer so the same spend also retires Meridian's AWS Enterprise Discount Program commitment.
negotiation_language: This is a routing change, not a price change -- same dollars, same vendor relationship, but it counts toward two commitments instead of one.
vendor_give: Structural only; Databricks' AWS Marketplace desk handles this as a standard private-offer amendment.
timing_dependency: Attach to the Year 2 amendment; not urgent on its own.
risk_if_ignored: Not a hard deadline, but a standing missed structural advantage every year it is not in place.
